plain_language_description: A mechanism that declines to produce an answer or perform an action.
interpretive_boundary: Distinguish a described or proposed refusal from its implementation, use and evaluated performance.

plain_language_description: A mechanism that blocks an output from being released.
interpretive_boundary: Post hoc identification of a harmful output does not by itself establish blocking.

plain_language_description: A mechanism that restricts the scope within which the agent may operate.
interpretive_boundary: A listed task or predefined command set alone is not proof of an enforced safety boundary.

plain_language_description: Permissions governing which tools or actions the agent may execute.
interpretive_boundary: Tool availability, function schemas or a sandbox alone do not establish enforceable authorization.

plain_language_description: Controls on access using identity, role or execution authorization.
interpretive_boundary: Local execution, de-identification and research-data access are not automatically agent access control.

plain_language_description: A human decision is required before an output or action proceeds.
interpretive_boundary: Post hoc expert assessment is not a runtime approval gate.

plain_language_description: A defined condition triggers escalation to another actor or process.
interpretive_boundary: Record actual escalation functionality separately from recommendations to consult a clinician.

plain_language_description: A mechanism permits an ongoing agent action or workflow to be overridden or interrupted.
interpretive_boundary: Human observation without an ability to affect the workflow is not sufficient.

plain_language_description: A limit or termination control with an explicit failure-loop or safety-protection purpose.
interpretive_boundary: Generic token, iteration or efficiency budgets are not sufficient. Retrying does not prove an upper limit.

plain_language_description: An operational action restores or reverts a prior runtime state.
interpretive_boundary: Rollback policy or approval belongs to governance; do not conflate policy with runtime execution.

plain_language_description: A mechanism intercepts potential information leakage during operation.
interpretive_boundary: Privacy claims or local execution alone are not evidence of interception.

plain_language_description: Logging used to support governance audit or accountability for agent activity.
interpretive_boundary: Experimental traces qualify only when their purpose and function support auditing; no additional tamper-proof requirement is imposed.

plain_language_description: Traceability of agent outputs to evidence sources or of artifacts to their versions.
interpretive_boundary: Explicit output-to-source links may qualify without simultaneous version governance; arbitrary traces are not automatically provenance.

plain_language_description: Assignment of responsibility for the agent or its lifecycle activities.
interpretive_boundary: Authorship alone does not establish an operational responsibility assignment.

plain_language_description: A process for reporting incidents involving the agent.
interpretive_boundary: Distinguish a proposed process from implemented reporting.

plain_language_description: An approval process governing release of an agent or system version.
interpretive_boundary: A publication or code release alone does not establish a release-approval control.

plain_language_description: A process governing changes to the agent or its relevant artifacts.
interpretive_boundary: Describe approval or control separately from merely observing that a version changed.

plain_language_description: Monitoring for changes in data, operation or performance over time.
interpretive_boundary: A one-time robustness test is not automatically ongoing drift monitoring.

plain_language_description: Testing after an update to detect deterioration or unintended changes.
interpretive_boundary: A baseline comparison alone is not evidence of a post-update testing process.

plain_language_description: Repeated validation according to a periodic lifecycle process.
interpretive_boundary: Initial validation does not establish periodic revalidation.

plain_language_description: Monitoring of the agent after deployment.
interpretive_boundary: Proposed monitoring and offline experiments are not evidence of deployed surveillance.

plain_language_description: Governance review of access rights or authorization.
interpretive_boundary: Distinguish review of permissions from runtime enforcement of permissions.

plain_language_description: Institutional oversight of relevant agent responsibilities, authorization or lifecycle controls.
interpretive_boundary: Research ethics approval qualifies only when its scope supports the agent-governance claim; a dedicated committee is not required.
